questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere where I had a chance of understanding the local language. I moved to Denmark to study and I wanted to experience another one of the Scandinavian countries. I also wanted to go somewhere that I could get the courses that I needed

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easier than expected. I was afraid that it would be very difficult, but the University of Bergen and Sammen made it very easy for the exchange students to get oriented.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't recieve any special assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was very easy to find housing through
Sammen.no
.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Sammen makes it very easy to find housing, but you might get a shared room with one of the same gender and common kitchen. I think that there is a housing guarantee for exchange students. They are used to exchange students, and they facilitate the processes for exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a course catalogue with information about the courses' content, requirements, exams and so on. Then you register for the course on studentweb, and you can change courses after about a month where you can try out the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always write to the faculty for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't really have any general advice. The information is on the university's website. If you want to take a course with Norwegian as the teaching language, you need to write to the faculty and then they make the course visible in the registration website

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my courses were BA-level and it was a level that I could follow

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EUR101 - Europeisk historie og politikk
Sampol116 - Democracy and Democratization
Sampol238 - The Politics of Contestation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The politics of contestation was very interesting, because it focuses on the different cleavages that divide voters. Also Democracy an Democratization was very interesting because it looks at the state of democracy in the worlds with a comparative perspective, and you learn about autocratization and democratization.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There wasn't really anything. I went on trips that I didn't know I wanted to before I went to Bergen, so renting a car was an an unexpected cost

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food wasn't as bad as I had expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different associations. Orchestras, choirs different academic and faculty social associations.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking is a must. I didn't join any association, except for an orchestra, which I liked very much, but I imagine that the different associations  also are a way to get into contact with people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Trolltunga, Kjeragbolten, a cabin trip maybe. A lot of people also went to Lofoten, and a train trip to Oslo.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I lived with international students in a shared flat/common kitchen, so mu friends were mostly internationals. I joined an orchestra and there I got to speak a little Norwegian. Being from a Nordic country, it wasn't so hard to adjust to another Scandinavian country.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think that joining an association or soe social activity is probably the easiest way to get into contact with local students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't really have any big challenging cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciate the Norwegian language, and the nature. It is also a very active country where hiking and the gym is a bit part of a lot of peoples daily life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Even though it is important to study, don't forget to have fun and have a lot of new experiences and trips. 
For me, living in a shared flat, even though it was a shared room was a great part of the exchange, you get so close with the other people that you live with. 
The university has very good facilities for studying. Try out the different faculties' libraries and study spots. The social sciences library was open 24 hours if you have a student card during the exam season

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sammen is very helpful or a lot of aspects of life as a student in Bergen. It is not only housing but also the cafeterias at the Uni, many gyms, help to go to the doctor and the dentist and so on.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The connections you make with other people. Living together with other people becoming friends while being away from your normal life creates a special bond.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Prioritising your studies while also having an active and social daily life, going out with friends, going on hikes and trips.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
